newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd rebels deny killing Turkish teachers.
newsitem.headline: Kurd rebels deny killing Turkish teachers.

text.p: The political wing of the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) on Wednesday denied Turkey's accusations that its guerrillas had killed four teachers, blaming security forces for the deaths.

The pro-Kurdish DEM news agency quoted an official of the Kurdistan National Liberation Front (ERNK) as saying Turkish authorities had engineered Tuesday's shootings in a hamlet of Diyarbakir province and then blamed PKK separatists.
"ERNK's European organisation said that the PKK had nothing to do with the killing of the four teachers in Diyarbakir," the Cologne-based agency said.
Armed assailants abducted seven teachers in the southeastern village of Hantepe early on Tuesday and shot four dead by the nearby Tigris River.
Security officials blamed the rebels. DEM quoted an unnamed spokesman as saying security forces were behind the attack and that government forces had been in control of the village.
Human rights group Amnesty International said on Tuesday that rebels had killed 90 teachers in their 12-year fight for autonomy or independence in southeast Turkey.
More than 20,000 people have died in the conflict.
